title: Holding cells flayed; Inquest probes woman's suicide
article: The death of a suicidal Nelson House woman while in police custody is sparking a call for the closure of all band-operated holding cells on reserves.
Rachel Lori Wood, 22, was found hanging from the bars of a band office holding cell door shortly after 8 a.m. on Oct. 5, 2003, less than one hour after she was arrested.
Wood died alone in a squalid cell whose cross-work bars made it easy for her to hang herself, said provincial court Judge Murray Thompson in a 78-page inquest report released yesterday.

"After viewing photographs of (the cells) I could only describe them as inhumane and disgusting," Thompson said. "They were not fit to house anyone, certainly not anyone who was feeling depressed or suicidal."

Wood had been drinking for several hours when she became distraught and suicidal following a fight with her boyfriend, the inquest was told last November. Worried friends called band police and she was lodged in a holding cell to sober up.
The inquest heard the cells were not monitored by cameras and were not visible from the guard desk. Cell toilets could not be flushed and were filled with human waste.
Thompson made nine recommendations in his report, including replacing all band operated holding cells with new cells that meet RCMP standards. RCMP holding cell doors are made of solid metal.
Other recommendations include providing mandatory suicide prevention training for band police and installing closed circuit cameras in all holding cells.
At the time Wood took her life, the only person on duty at the station was a dispatcher working her second shift with no training. A full-time guard had been previously laid off.

The inquest was told band constables and auxiliary constables often worked up to 72 hours without a break. Auxiliary constables received no formal training and would routinely fill in for regular band constables when they didn't turn up for work, often after a payday weekend.
An auxiliary constable told the inquest he had been working more than 34 hours straight when he took Wood into custody.
